newsitem.title: JORDAN: Arab Bank backs $100 mln Jordan eurobond.
newsitem.headline: Arab Bank backs $100 mln Jordan eurobond.

text.p: Jordan's Arab Bank has set up a local bank syndicate to underwrite part of a planned $100 million eurobond issue by Jordan Phosphate Mines, the country's first corporate bond issue, bankers said on Wednesday.
They said Arab Bank had formed the syndicate to negotiate with an international bank which will be awarded the mandate to lead manage the bond issue in capital markets.
Jordan Phosphate Mines Co wants to tap international markets to part finance an estimated $250 million project to expand the firm's major Shidiyah mine.

Seven global investment banks have been shortlisted by Jordan Phosphate Mines with the guidance of Jordan's central bank and the World Bank. They have been given a May 15 deadline to submit offers for a $100 million floating rate note.
The seven shortlisted bidders are HSBC Markets, ING Barings, Union Bank of Switzerland, Paribas, ANZ Grindlays, Citibank, and Merrill Lynch.

The lead manager will be announced in early June and should arrange the floating of the issue whose pricing and maturity has still not been decided, bankers said. It is also expected to underwrite the remainder of the issue not covered by the Jordanian syndicate.
"We want to make the issue successful and allow Jordanian banks to take a significant portion of the issue," said one Jordanian banker.

Bankers say Jordanian banks could underwrite as much as 50 percent of the issue. The role of Arab Bank, one of the Middle East's biggest financial institutions, in negotiating on behalf of banks should give more confidence to the lead manager and boost Jordanian banks' standing internationally, they said.
